name: Facial Dysmorphism-Corpus Callosum Hypoplasia-Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy
aliases: Facial Dysmorphism with Corpus Callosum Hypoplasia and Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for FD-CC Hypoplasia-Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Neuroimaging evidence of corpus callosum hypoplasia or agenesis on MRI
Onset of refractory infantile epileptic encephalopathy with multiple seizure types before 2 years of age
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes (e.g., KCNQ2, STXBP1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (facial dysmorphism, corpus callosum hypoplasia, and infantile epileptic encephalopathy) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: thin or small brain connection between hemispheres

pathognomonic.notes: Includes hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Multiple seizure types including spasms and tonic seizures
searchTerms: refractory epileptic brain disorder in babies

common.notes: Delayed milestones in motor and cognitive domains
searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

common.symptomName: Abnormal EEG with multifocal epileptiform discharges
common.notes: Electroencephalogram abnormalities typical of epileptic encephalopathy
searchTerms: abnormal brain wave test with multiple seizure spots
irregular electrical brain activity on EEG

rare.notes: Possibly secondary to hypotonia and aspiration

laboratory: Elevated lactate in some cases indicating mitochondrial dysfunction
imaging: MRI showing corpus callosum hypoplasia or agenesis
Possible cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
other: Abnormal EEG with multifocal epileptiform discharges and burst suppression pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly neonatal onset seizures without characteristic facial dysmorphism
Normal corpus callosum on imaging in many cases
Corpus callosum agenesis without infantile epileptic encephalopathy
Absence of characteristic facial dysmorphic features
Severe epileptic encephalopathy with STXBP1 mutations but variable facial features
Corpus callosum may be normal or mildly affected

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures within first 6 months of life
Severe developmental regression following seizure onset
Neuroimaging showing corpus callosum hypoplasia combined with dysmorphic facial features
references: Orphanet: Facial Dysmorphism-Corpus Callosum Hypoplasia-Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy, ORPHA:708171
